To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

miR 146 is a NF kB dependent microRNA, which is induced by microbial products and proinflammatory stimuli and which is predicted to target the 3'UTR of IL1R associated kinase 1, a key signaling molecule downstream of Toll like receptors and IL 1.

microRNA 146 is induced in response to microbial components and inflammatory stimuli and that it targets two key signaling molecules in innate immune responses, IL 1 receptor-associated kinase 1 and tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6.

NF kB dependent induction of two microRNAs (miR 132 and miR 154) and one miRNA cluster (miR 155) is a common feature in innate and acquired immune cells in response to a wide range of microbial and inflammatory stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a novel microRNA that is induced by microbial components and pro inflammatory cytokines and that is predicted to down regulate two key adapter molecules of the Toll like receptor and the cytokine receptor signaling pathway.
the identification of novel microRNAs and their target genes in innate and acquired immune response pathways.
the identification and characterization of microRNAs as negative regulators of the innate immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NF kB dependent miR 146 is induced upon activation of innate immune signaling, and that miR 146 targets the adapter molecules of the innate immune signaling pathways, thereby acting as a negative feedback mechanism to terminate signaling.
microRNAs are a new class of genes that are regulated by NFkB.
the miR 146 gene is a novel NF kB dependent gene, which is induced by a variety of microbial and inflammatory stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NF kB is a key transcription factor that controls expression of miR 145/146.
NF kB activation in monocytes induces miR 146 expression, which in turn down regulates the expression of two important signaling components of innate immune responses, IRAK1 and TRAF6.
miR 146 is induced by NF kB, and it targets two key adapter molecules in Toll like and cytokines signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microRNAs can act as negative regulators of innate immune signaling and that their induction by microbial stimuli may be part of the innate immune system response.
miR 146 is an endotoxin responsive microRNA and is regulated by the transcription factor NF kB, a key regulator of innate and acquired immune functions.
miR 146 is a new component of the innate immune response.
